newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight recovers as liquidity crunch persists.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight recovers as liquidity crunch persists.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate recovered from Tuesday's sharp drop as a liquidity crunch pressured rates upward, dealers said.
They said the overnight rate rose to 8.3 percent from the opening of 7.5 percent before settling at 7.7/8.0 percent around 0730 GMT. It closed at 6.0 percent on Tuesday.
"Yesterday was an aberration. The overnight had dropped because of some temporary mismatch caused by the power breakdown," a dealer with a local bank said.
Dealers said Bank Negara, through its agents, was lending in the overnight market at 8.5 percent on Tuesday, when a power failure affected several parts of the city, including the central bank.

Some banks squared up in a hurry and when power returned, some large banks, who are principal dealers for the central bank, were holding excess funds. This pulled down the overnight towards the close, the dealers said.
"But, the crunch is not so bad today because some people are covering longer-term," another dealer said.
Longer tenures of two months to one year were unchanged at 7.35/40 percent on mild demand.
However, short-end funds were slightly weaker, with one- and two-week money at 7.40/50 percent against 7.80/90, three-week at 7.35/45 against 7.40/50.

Dealers said the market was expected to remain tight until next Wednesday, when a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill matures. "It depends on whether (Bank) Negara rolls over the bill or not," a dealer with another local bank said.
